onboarding.title: Designing LSE CRM around Real Users

overview.text: Lasenda, an accounting service company, faced major operational inefficiencies due to limitations of their existing CRM, Hawksoft. The system lacked essential task-tracking capabilities, making it difficult to monitor employee progress and manage workloads. Weak data encryption posed security concerns for sensitive financial information. additionally, Hawksoft provided no reliable method for handling client deadlines, increasing the risk of delays and compliance issues.

onboarding.problem: "Outdated CRM causes major inefficiency, security risks, and missed deadlines."

goal.title: Transforming workflow through secure, tailored software.
goal.text:
• Develop a secure, centralized system tailored to Lasenda's workflow.
  • Enable clear tracking of employee tasks, workloads and project progress.
  • Implement stronger data protection and encryption measures for financial information.
  • introduced automated, reliable client-deadline management to reduce missed submission.
  • Create a flexible develipment process that adapts to evolving stakeholder needs.

discover.text: To gain a deep understanding of Lasenda's operational challenges and user needs, a 5 day interview based research phase was conducted with key stakeholders and end users. These sessions focused on uncovering daily workflows, identifying pain points within the existing Hawksoft system, and understanding unmet requirements related to task management, data security and deadline handling. Insights gathered from these interviews directly informed the product requirements and helped prioritized features that would deliver the greatest impact in the LSE system.

define.text:
Background
Lasenda, an accounting services company, was experiencing operational inefficiencies due to limitations in their existing CRM system. After conducting stakeholder interviews (Super Admin, Admin, Supervisor, and Employees), I created a journey map to visualize the current workflow and uncover pain points across roles.The journey map captures the end-to-end process from client onboarding to task completion, highlighting breakdowns in task tracking, deadline management, and data security.

Key User Roles Identified

  • Customer – New or existing client 
  • Super Admin – Manages onboarding and system-level actions
  • Admin – Handles profile creation and account setup
  • Supervisor – Assigns and monitors tasks
  • Employee – Executes accounting tasks

Client Onboarding - Pain Points
  • Manual data entry
  • No structured onboarding flow
  • Difficult to manage multiple account types
  • Risk of incomplete or inconsistent information

Assign to Supervisor - Pain Points
  • No clear visibility of assignment history
  • Difficult to track supervisor workload
  • Limited progress transparency

Assign to Staff Member - Pain Points
  • Cannot assign tasks to multiple departments efficiently
  • No real-time task tracking
  • Hard to monitor progress
  • No automated notifications for new assignments

Task Completion - Pain Points
  • No structured deadline management
  • No automated reminders
  • Limited performance monitoring
  • Risk of delayed compliance submissions

Insights:

There is no centralized way to track task status, employee workload, or assignment flow. This reduces accountability and transparency.The absence of automated deadline tracking increases the risk of delays and compliance issues.Weak encryption mechanisms create risks when handling sensitive financial data.The workflow depends heavily on manual coordination between roles, increasing operational friction.

 Opportunity Areas:
  • Introduce structured onboarding forms
  • Enable task progress tracking dashboards
  • Add deadline management with automated notifications
  • Support multi-department assignment
  • Implement stronger data encryption
  • Auto-generate client IDs and agreement documents
  • Centralize relevant regulatory links

design.intro:
After clearly defining the core problems during the Define phase,  including poor task visibility, weak deadline management, and security concerns, I transitioned into the Design phase with a focused objective:To create a structured, secure, and transparent CRM experience that improves workflow efficiency across all roles.

During this phase, I focused on:

  • Designing a clearer task assignment and tracking system
  • Improving deadline visibility with automated notifications
  • Creating structured onboarding flows
  • Strengthening data handling touch points
  • Enhancing role based dashboards for better transparency
